title: Decoupling Monoliths: Strategies for Java Developers
summary: A deep dive into migrating legacy Java monoliths to microservices architectures using Spring Boot.
content:
Migrating from a monolithic architecture to microservices is a journey, not a sprint. For Java developers, this often means breaking down large EAR/WAR deployments into smaller, independent Spring Boot applications.

Key Strategies:

  • Identify Domains: Use Domain-Driven Design (DDD) to find natural boundaries.
  • Strangler Fig Pattern: Slowly replace specific functionality with new services.
  • Database Refactoring: This is the hardest part. decoupling the data layer is crucial.

title: Angular Performance at Scale
summary: Tips for optimizing large frontend applications: Lazy loading, Change Detection strategies, and more.
content:
When building large-scale Angular applications, performance can degrade quickly if not managed proactively.

Top Tips:

  • OnPush Change Detection: Switch to `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush` by default.
  • Lazy Loading: Split your app into feature modules and load them on demand.
  • RxJS Best Practices: Avoid memory leaks by properly unsubscribing from observables.

title: The Art of Clean Code
summary: Reflections on maintainability, SOLID principles, and why writing code for humans is more important than for machines.
content:
"Any fool can write code that a computer can understand. Good programmers write code that humans can understand." - Martin Fowler.

Clean code is about readability and maintainability. It's about respecting the next developer who will touch your code (which might be you in 6 months).

title: Why Terminals Never Die
summary: A meta-post about why I chose this retro aesthetic for my portfolio.
content:
There is a timeless elegance to the command line. It represents direct control, lack of distraction, and pure utility. This portfolio is an homage to the tools we use every day.

Green text on a black background isn't just a style; it's a lifestyle.

title: Managing Distributed Teams
summary: Insights on leadership, asynchronous communication, and building culture remotely.
content:
Remote work is here to stay. Managing distributed teams requires a shift from presence-based management to outcome-based management.

Core Principles:

  • Over-communicate: Content is easily lost in text.
  • Trust your team: Focus on results, not hours.
